    public interface IMessageHandler
    A message handler is designed to consume and process PorticoMessage subclass objects, performing any appropraite actions (whether that be doing nothing, tranforming the message somehow, taking some action with the information contained within the message, filling out a ResponseMessage, etc...).

    To be considered valid, a message handler must both implement this interface and declare the MessageHandler annotation (providing all the necessary configuration information).

    RECOMMENDED: Unless you have an excellent reason, it is *STRONGLY* recommended that all your message handlers extend the LRCMessageHandler class. It provides a number of useful helper methods and during initialization it will cache locally a number of useful LRC resources for easy access.

    NOTE: All IMessageHandler implementations should have either NO CONSTRUCTOR or a PUBLIC, NO-ARG CONSTRUCTOR. This is due to the fact that handler instances will generally be created through reflection (with the name of the implementation being obtained from a configuration file).

    • Method Detail

      • initialize

        void initialize(Map<String,Object> properties)
         throws JConfigurationException
        The handler should execute all its initialization code in this method. It can be passed a Map instance containing whatever necessary configuration data the application using the messaging framework thinks it needs. Included in the properties at all times will be a link to the MessageSink the handler is being added to under the key LRCProperties.KEY_LRC.

        If a fatal error occurs during configuration, the handler should throw a JConfigurationException and this will cause the messaging framework to stop processing.

        Throws:
        JConfigurationException

      • process

        void process(MessageContext context)
      throws Exception
        Process the message information found in the given MessageContext and take an appropriate course of action. If an error occurs, an exception should be thrown. You can declare your handler to throw application specific checked-exceptions (or to throw no exceptions at all).
        Parameters:
        context - The MessageContext that contains the information to be processed.
        Throws:
        Exception

      • getName

        String getName()
        Each handler must have a name. Return the name.

      • setName

        void setName(String name)
        Set the name for this handler. If the name is provided in the MessageHandler annotation, this method will be automatically called by the framework. If not, the class should provide a default name.

      • isAugmentable

        boolean isAugmentable()
        Returns true if this handler can be extended into a MessageChain if another handler wishes to handle the same message type. False if not. If it can be augmented, the relative position of the handlers is decided by their priority.

      • setAugmentable

        void setAugmentable(boolean augmentable)
        Set the augmentable status for this handler. (see isAugmentable())

      • getPriority

        int getPriority()
        If the handler isAugmentable() and is extended into a chain, the relative position of the handlers depends on their priority. The higher the priority, the earlier in the chain they will appear. This value should be between 1 and 10 (anything over 10 is assumed to be 10 and anything under 1 is assumed to be 1). This value should be provided in the MessageHandler annotation (defaults to 5) and this method will be called by the framework.

      • setPriority

        void setPriority(int priority)
        Sets the priority for the handler, see getPriority() for more information.
